summary: Facepalm: Facepalm scan for 2026-10-03 (window Sept 27–Oct 3). I'm submitting no candidates. Web search ran out after about 30 queries. I then used Fox News's daily HTML sitemaps (Sept 27–Oct 3) to find in-window stories, until the fetch limit also ran out. None of the stories I found had two accepted publishers that I had actually opened. Every in-window lead failed for one of these reasons: one accepted source only, outlets not on the list, a crime with a victim, or a party that isn't currently allowed. The one close Democratic political item, Fetterman's slip, happened on Sept 26, one day before the window. Genius: Genius scan for 2026-10-03 (window Sept 27 to Oct 3): no candidates submitted. The search tool limit was hit early, after only a few searches and one page opened (the Space.com September archive). No story in the window could be checked against two accepted publishers or matched to a verbatim quote from a page I had opened. The window's Space.com items were already used or set aside on earlier days (Starship Flight 14, Crew-13, the fire amoeba, the cold lava world, Little Red Dots, wandering black holes). The other science items I found were led outside the US or dated after the scan date. Leaving the side empty instead of proposing unverified stories. No genius or facepalm story met the standard; nothing published.

candidates.headline: Sen. John Fetterman calls himself a 'lifelong Republican' at the Texas Tribune Festival, then corrects himself
candidates.reason: Happened Saturday, Sept 26, 2026, one day before the 7-day window. I opened only one accepted source (Fox News) before tool capacity ran out.

candidates.headline: Sen. Eric Schmitt accuses Jack Smith of perjury after mixing up the Iowa Hawkeyes and the Atlanta Hawks
candidates.reason: Subject is a Republican, and Republican political facepalm stories aren't currently allowed. It was also set aside earlier for lack of a second accepted source.

candidates.headline: Judge orders New York City to void and redo its pied-à-terre tax notices over procedural errors
candidates.reason: A contested court ruling now on appeal (the city says an automatic stay applies), not a self-evident blunder. I opened only one accepted source (Fox News).

candidates.headline: Knox County, Ind., voting machines reprogrammed a third time after a ballot error
candidates.reason: In the date window (Oct 2), but all coverage found was on outlets not on the accepted list (WWBL, WZDM, MyWabashValley, Sun-Commercial, a Yahoo republication).

candidates.headline: Packaging error leads to double ballots in a Lancaster County, Pa., township
candidates.reason: The only copy found was on Yahoo, which isn't allowed, and the page couldn't be opened to confirm the date or original publisher.

candidates.headline: Kendall County, Ill., sends 300 wrong mail-in ballots to two precincts
candidates.reason: Reported Oct 9, 2026, after the scan date, by Shaw Local, which isn't on the accepted list.

candidates.headline: Kanawha County, W.Va., TikTok couple charged with arson in an abandoned-house fire
candidates.reason: Crime with a victim other than the perpetrators (a nearby church was damaged).

candidates.headline: Texas man arrested after police say he drove into a closed Kroger to use the bathroom
candidates.reason: Property crime with a victim other than the perpetrator (the store).

candidates.headline: Man gets stuck in blackberry bushes during a Pierce County, Wash., deputies' call
candidates.reason: Came from a domestic disturbance call involving a knife threat against a roommate, so there is a crime victim. Only one accepted source (Fox 13 Seattle).

candidates.headline: Error on North Carolina jury duty website exposes Social Security numbers and medical records
candidates.reason: Reported Sept 24, 2026, before the 7-day window. People's personal data was exposed.

candidates.headline: New America.gov government hub contains hidden 'surprises'
candidates.reason: Federal (Republican) administration story, and that party isn't currently allowed. It also appears to be intentional, not a blunder.

candidates.headline: Sunrise-III balloon observatory reveals fine magnetic structures above the quiet sun
candidates.reason: Led by the National Astronomical Observatory of Japan; no US lead institution. The only page seen was phys.org (Sept 30).

candidates.headline: Laser-made muons used to image dense objects for the first time
candidates.reason: Work done at the ELI-NP facility in Romania by a Romanian-led team; not in the US. It is also an arXiv preprint.

candidates.headline: Karl Deisseroth shares 2026 Nobel Prize in medicine for optogenetics
candidates.reason: Announced in October after the 2026-10-03 scan date; outside the window.

candidates.headline: Caltech physicists measure a quantum energy ladder predicted 40 years ago
candidates.reason: Already set aside on Sept 28: the Nature paper and Caltech announcement are from Aug 19, 2026, and the ScienceDaily write-up is not the event date.

candidates.headline: Swiss glaciers lose more than 5% of their ice in a year (NPR, Sept 30)
candidates.reason: Not in the US, and a measurement of loss, not an achievement.

candidates.headline: Startup seeks to prove embryo gene editing is safe (NPR, Sept 29)
candidates.reason: A company's plans and funding, not an achieved result; 'could one day' territory.

candidates.headline: Early mammal predecessor could swim, suckle and swallow (Nature news)
candidates.reason: The Nature news page appears to be dated after the scan date. The lead institution and a second accepted source were not checked before the search tool limit was reached.

candidates.headline: World's loudest bird could drown out a rock concert (Science News)
candidates.reason: The Science News page appears to be dated after the scan date. The study location (likely outside the US) and a second source were not checked before the tool limit was reached.
